ev.isl_m_adhan.text.1: It is still dark, but the muezzin's voice already drifts down from the minaret. Shutters clap open somewhere, a water jug clinks - the city is waking up.
ev.isl_m_adhan.text.2: At sunset voices from a dozen minarets call across the rooftops as if arguing over whose is lovelier. You stopped in the middle of the street to listen.
ev.isl_m_hammam_child.text: Your first time at the hammam: hot marble, clouds of steam, light falling through little star-shaped holes in the dome. The attendant scrubbed you with a rough mitt until you squealed, and then you got cold sherbet.
ev.isl_m_hammam_news.text: Women's day at the hammam. Henna, combs and talk until evening: who is matchmaking whom, whose maid ran off, whose daughter-in-law is putting on airs. You came home clean and full of news.
ev.isl_m_spice_suq.text: The spice row smells so strong it makes your head spin: pepper, cinnamon, saffron, cloves from faraway seas. A trader let you sniff a nutmeg and said it was worth more than silver.
ev.isl_m_paper.text: On the booksellers' street they sell paper - smooth, pale and far cheaper than parchment. You bought a few sheets and hesitated a long time before spoiling them with the first letters.
ev.isl_m_boat_bridge.text: The bridge over the Tigris is boats chained together with planks laid across them. It sways underfoot, boatmen dart beneath it, and in the middle it smells of the river and grilled fish.
ev.isl_m_nilometer.text: Criers walk the streets calling out how many cubits the water has risen at the Nilometer on Rawda Island. Sixteen cubits - and the city rejoices: there will be a harvest, there will be bread.
ev.isl_m_umayyad_mosque.text: In the courtyard of the Great Mosque the golden mosaics blaze in the sun: rivers, trees, palaces - they say it shows the gardens of Paradise. You sat by the fountain and gazed until someone called you home.
ev.isl_m_damascus_blade.text: A swordsmith showed you a blade patterned like ripples on water and sliced a silk scarf in mid-air. "The steel comes from India, but the secret of the tempering is ours," he winked.
ev.isl_m_rosewater.text: At dawn you gathered Damascene roses before the dew dried. Then the petals steamed in a copper still over the fire, and rose water trickled out drop by drop. The whole house smelled of it for a week.
ev.isl_m_mezquita.text: Inside the Great Mosque, rows of red-and-white arches stretch away like a palm grove made of stone. Hundreds of brass lamps, coolness, silence. You got lost among the columns - and don't regret it.
ev.isl_m_cordoba_library.text: They say the caliph's library holds so many books that the catalogue alone fills dozens of notebooks. A copyist you know led you past the shelves - and you realised you would never read even a hundredth of it.
ev.isl_m_noria.text: The water wheel creaks day and night, lifting water into the channels between the orange trees. You learned to fall asleep to that creak - and to wake if it ever falls silent.
ev.isl_m_bosphorus.text: A caique boatman rowed you across the Bosphorus. The current pulls toward the Sea of Marmara, dolphins surface by the side, and on the shore stand cypresses and white minarets.
ev.isl_m_grand_bazaar.text: You could wander under the vaults of the Grand Bazaar all day: rows of jewellers, carpet sellers, armourers, money changers. Three times you were invited to sit for a drink, twice someone tried to shortchange you.
ev.isl_m_tulips.text: The tulips are blooming in the garden - slender and pointed like daggers. A neighbour swears a bulb of a rare variety sells for the price of a horse. You don't believe him, but now you count your bulbs.
ev.isl_m_coffee_first.text: For the first time someone poured you coffee - a black, bitter, scalding drink from Yemen. At first you winced, and then you couldn't sleep till midnight and chatted with the neighbours like never before.
ev.isl_m_shadow_play.text: In the evening a lamp was lit behind a stretched cloth, and leather puppets came to life: a cunning servant fooled a greedy judge. You laughed so hard your cheeks hurt afterwards.
ev.isl_m_storyteller.text: A storyteller in the square tells of a clever girl who saved her life for a thousand nights with stories. At the best part he fell silent and held out a cup for coins. You'll come back tomorrow.
ev.isl_m_calligrapher.text: The calligrapher cut the tip of his reed pen at a slant, dipped it in soot ink - and the letters flowed across the page like a dance. "First the hand, then the soul," he said without looking up.
ev.isl_m_caravan_arrives.text: A caravan has reached the caravanserai: hundreds of camels, the jingle of bells, dust up to the sky. The drivers tell of sandstorms while the merchants are already laying out indigo and frankincense.
ev.isl_m_henna_night.text: The henna night before a neighbour's wedding. The bride's palms are painted with patterns, the women sing and beat tambourines, and they drew a flower on your fingers too. It lasted almost a month.
ev.isl_m_mawlid.text: The Prophet's birthday: streets hung with lanterns, reciters chanting verses, sugar dolls and horses for sale in the market. You begged for a sugar horse and kept it until the ants found it.
ev.isl_m_snow_sherbet.text: On a hot day sherbet was served with snow. The snow is brought from the mountains of Syria by ship and camel for the sultan's table, and a little reaches the great houses. Cold on your tongue in the middle of a Cairo summer - a true miracle.
ev.isl_m_sabil.text: In the heat you drank from a street fountain, a sabil. Above the grille is carved the name of the man who built it for God and for people many years ago. The water still flows.
ev.isl_m_dhimmi_dress.text: A decree has reminded everyone who is not Muslim to wear a special belt and colours. In the market people glance at you more than usual. You hold your head high: your faith is who you are.
ev.isl_m_ghitas.text: The night of the Copts' Epiphany: thousands of torches and candles on the Nile bank, people dip into the river, and Muslims come to watch and celebrate alongside everyone. The water glitters like molten gold.
ev.isl_m_baghdad_ruins.text: Old men point to empty lots where palaces and libraries stood before the Mongols came. The city goes on living, trading and praying, but people speak of the old Baghdad as of someone who has died.
ev.isl_m_oud.text: In the courtyard someone played a five-stringed oud - they say the famous musician Ziryab added the fifth string. The song was about parting, and even the cat on the roof stopped washing itself.
ev.isl_m_bimaristan.text: You visited an acquaintance at the bimaristan. Treatment is free, paid for by an endowment; musicians play at night for patients who can't sleep, and those discharged get a little money for their first days.
ev.isl_m_istanbul_1453.text: An old neighbour tells how, in the year the city fell, Sultan Mehmed rode into Hagia Sophia and ordered it made a mosque. The Greeks listen in silence - they have their own memory of that day.
ev.isl_m_simit.text: A vendor with a tray on his head is shouting down the street - he has sesame bread rings, still warm. You shared one with a friend and spent ages picking sesame seeds off your palm.
ev.isl_d_hajj.title: The Hajj
ev.isl_d_hajj.text: A pilgrim caravan is gathering for Mecca. The road will take months: desert, wells, Bedouin, the crush around the Kaaba. But whoever completes the Hajj comes home with the honoured title of hajji.
ev.isl_d_hajj.go.success: You circled the Kaaba, stood on the plain of Arafat and came home a different person. The neighbours met you with drums.
ev.isl_d_hajj.go.failure: A fever struck you on the road. You reached Mecca, but came home sick and thin.
ev.isl_d_hajj.note: The Hajj to Mecca is one of the five pillars of Islam: everyone healthy and able to afford the journey should make it at least once. Great pilgrim caravans set out from Baghdad, Damascus and Cairo.
ev.isl_d_hajj_later.title: A hajji's word
ev.isl_d_hajj_later.text: The neighbours remember your Hajj. Two men have quarrelled over a boundary and come to you: "Judge between us, hajji - we'll trust you."
ev.isl_d_fast_heat.title: Fasting in the heat
ev.isl_d_fast_heat.text: Ramadan has fallen in the fiercest heat. Sunset is far off, your lips are cracked, and the work won't wait. Someone nearby whispers that heavy labour is a valid reason to postpone the fast.
ev.isl_d_fast_heat.rest: Work only in the morning and lose wages
ev.isl_d_fast_heat.break: Postpone the fast and make it up in winter
ev.isl_d_zakat.title: Zakat
ev.isl_d_zakat.text: A year has passed and it is time to give zakat - a fortieth of your savings - for the poor, debtors and travellers. The collector is waiting, and a merchant you know advises you to "count modestly".
ev.isl_d_zakat.direct: Hand it out yourself to the widows of the quarter
ev.isl_d_sufi.title: The Sufi lodge
ev.isl_d_sufi.text: At the dervish lodge they remember God at night: hundreds of voices repeat one word until it becomes breathing. The order's sheikh noticed you by the door and invited you in.
ev.isl_d_sufi.doubt: The theologians say this is excessive
ev.isl_f_laylat_qadr.title: The Night of Power
ev.isl_f_laylat_qadr.text: One of the last nights of Ramadan is the Night of Power, "better than a thousand months". The mosque is full until dawn as people pray for their fate in the year ahead.
ev.isl_d_jizya.title: The jizya
ev.isl_d_jizya.text: The poll-tax collector has come to the quarter. Christians and Jews - the "People of the Book" - are protected by law, but they pay the jizya. The collector demands more than usual and reads out your name loudly.
ev.isl_d_jizya.petition.success: The community head stepped in, and the extra was dropped.
ev.isl_d_jizya.petition.failure: The complaint did not help, and the collector remembered you.
ev.isl_d_jizya.note: Christians, Jews and Zoroastrians in Islamic lands were dhimmis, "protected people": they kept their faith and community courts, but paid the jizya poll tax and lived under restrictions.
ev.isl_d_convert_kin.title: The old community
ev.isl_d_convert_kin.text: Years have passed since you changed your faith. Your old neighbours in the quarter still turn away, but they have invited you to a wedding in their house all the same.
ev.isl_d_minority_office.title: A post in the divan
ev.isl_d_minority_office.text: The chancery, the divan, needs a literate accountant. Christians and Jews have served there for generations, but the chief hints: "A Muslim would find it easier to rise."
ev.isl_d_minority_office.serve.success: Your accounts proved the best in the divan. The post is yours.
ev.isl_d_minority_office.serve.failure: The post went to someone else. You were politely told "another time".
ev.isl_d_minority_office.convert: Embrace Islam and take the post
ev.isl_f_coptic_fast.title: The Coptic Great Fast
ev.isl_f_coptic_fast.text: The Copts fast for fifty-five days: no meat, milk or eggs, only beans, bread and onions. Muslim neighbours marvel: "Your fast is longer than ours!" The priest is gathering pilgrims for a desert monastery.
ev.isl_f_fire_temple.title: The last fire
ev.isl_f_fire_temple.text: The fire temple in your quarter is closing: its people would fit on a single street, and there's no money for firewood or a priest. The elders ask you to help carry the sacred fire into a home.
ev.isl_f_fire_temple.convert: Time to live like everyone around you
ev.isl_f_india_partner.title: A letter from Aden
ev.isl_f_india_partner.text: A fellow member of the community writes from Aden: he is sailing to India for pepper and seeks a partner in Fustat. Letters like this, like every paper bearing God's name, are never thrown away - they are laid in the synagogue's genizah.
ev.isl_f_india_partner.note: The genizah of the Ben Ezra synagogue in Fustat preserved hundreds of thousands of documents from the 10th-13th centuries: letters of merchants trading from Spain to India, contracts, lists, children's writing exercises.
ev.isl_f_india_letter.title: The pepper has come
ev.isl_f_india_letter.text: Your partner has come back from India alive, with pepper, betel and bronze ware. Your share is waiting. He is already planning another voyage.
ev.isl_f_india_letter.again.success: The second voyage did even better.
ev.isl_f_india_letter.again.failure: The ship met a storm off Malabar. Little came back.
ev.isl_f_mozarab.title: The martyrs of Córdoba
ev.isl_f_mozarab.text: The priest Eulogius urges Christians not to hide their faith: some go before the qadi and publicly denounce Islam, knowing they will be executed for it. The bishop begs people not to seek death. The young, meanwhile, speak Arabic better than Latin.
ev.isl_f_mozarab.speak.success: You spoke boldly but carefully, and no one touched you. The community respects you.
ev.isl_f_mozarab.speak.failure: You were seized and held in prison until the community raised the fine.
ev.isl_f_mozarab.adapt: Live like everyone else: language, dress, poetry
ev.isl_f_mozarab.note: Between 850 and 859 about fifty Christians in Córdoba were executed after deliberately denouncing Islam in public. They were inspired by the priest Eulogius, executed in 859; a church council of 852 urged Christians not to seek martyrdom.
ev.isl_f_church_mosque.title: The church becomes a mosque
ev.isl_f_church_mosque.text: Your parish church is being turned into a mosque: a crescent will go up over the dome and the frescoes will be painted over. The Patriarch advises going to the churches left to the Greeks. Before it closes, you are allowed to carry out the icons.
ev.isl_f_church_mosque.icons: Save the icons for the community
ev.isl_d_waqf.title: A waqf
ev.isl_d_waqf.text: The qadi suggests setting up a waqf: giving a house or shops in perpetuity so their income pays for a fountain, a school or a hospital. Your name will be carved over the door, and your descendants can manage the endowment.
ev.isl_d_waqf.keep: Leave the property to your heirs
ev.isl_d_waqf.note: A waqf is an inalienable charitable endowment in Islamic law. Waqf revenues kept mosques, madrasas, hospitals, fountains and caravanserais running across Islamic cities.
ev.isl_d_waqf_later.title: The school that bears your name
ev.isl_d_waqf_later.text: Orphans from the quarter study at your waqf school, and people bless you in the street. But the endowment's manager seems to be pocketing part of the income.
ev.isl_d_waqf_later.court: Take the manager to the qadi
ev.isl_d_waqf_later.court.success: The qadi replaced the manager. The school thrives.
ev.isl_d_waqf_later.court.failure: The manager found witnesses. The case dragged on and cost you money.
ev.isl_d_muhtasib.title: The muhtasib
ev.isl_d_muhtasib.text: The muhtasib, the market inspector, has come to the bazaar with his men. He checks weights, cloth and bread, and seats offenders backwards on a donkey. Your scales, it seems, are a little off.
ev.isl_d_muhtasib.honest: Admit it and fix the scales
ev.isl_d_muhtasib.bribe: Slip a coin to his assistant
ev.isl_d_muhtasib.bribe.success: The assistant looked away. You got off.
ev.isl_d_muhtasib.bribe.failure: The muhtasib saw it all. A fine, disgrace and a beating.
ev.isl_d_muhtasib.argue: Argue that the scales are true
ev.isl_d_muhtasib.argue.success: They reweighed in front of witnesses - it matched. The muhtasib apologised.
ev.isl_d_muhtasib.argue.failure: It didn't match. A fine and the neighbours' laughter.
ev.isl_d_qadi_court.title: A lawsuit
ev.isl_d_qadi_court.text: A neighbour claims you owe him for a donkey you bought, though you paid it all back. You could go to the qadi: you'll need two witnesses, and the judge will rule by sharia. Or you could call the elders and make peace.
ev.isl_d_qadi_court.qadi: Go to the qadi with witnesses
ev.isl_d_qadi_court.qadi.success: The witnesses confirmed it, and the qadi even awarded you compensation.
ev.isl_d_qadi_court.qadi.failure: One witness lost his nerve. The qadi ruled against you.
ev.isl_d_qadi_court.yield: Pay just to be rid of him
ev.isl_d_madrasa.title: The study circle
ev.isl_d_madrasa.text: At a pillar of the great mosque a famous scholar expounds hadith and law. His students write down his every word; to the best he gives an ijaza - written permission to teach others. Study costs money and years.
ev.isl_d_madrasa.text.cairo: At al-Azhar students from all over the world sit in circles around their teachers and sleep right there in the galleries. To the best the teacher gives an ijaza - written permission to teach others. Study costs money and years.
ev.isl_d_iqta.title: An iqta
ev.isl_d_iqta.text: The sultan grants you an iqta: the revenue of several villages. In return you must answer his first summons with mounted men. The villages are not yours forever - only while you serve.
ev.isl_d_iqta.text.istanbul: The sultan grants you a timar - the revenue of several villages in Rumelia. In return you must join campaigns mounted and armoured, with your own men. As long as you serve, the villages are yours.
ev.isl_d_iqta_campaign.title: The summons
ev.isl_d_iqta_campaign.text: A courier has brought the order: be at the camp with your horsemen within a month. Your villages pay so that you will fight.
ev.isl_d_iqta_campaign.go.success: The campaign went well. You came back with plunder and your commander's praise.
ev.isl_d_iqta_campaign.go.failure: An arrow wounded you in the very first skirmish, and you had to abandon your horse.
ev.isl_d_iqta_campaign.pay: Pay your way out and give up the iqta
ev.isl_d_mukataba.title: A contract of freedom
ev.isl_d_mukataba.text: The law lets a slave make a contract, a mukataba, with the master: pay your price in instalments and go free. The master may refuse, but it ill becomes a pious man.
ev.isl_d_mukataba.ask.success: The master signed the contract before two witnesses. Now every coin brings freedom closer.
ev.isl_d_mukataba.ask.failure: The master frowned: "Too soon for you." The conversation is over.
ev.isl_d_mukataba_paid.title: The last instalment
ev.isl_d_mukataba_paid.text: You handed over the last coin. The qadi recorded that you are free. By custom, your former master remains your patron.
ev.isl_d_mukataba_paid.craft: Set up on your own in the bazaar
ev.isl_d_mukataba_paid.stay: Stay on at your former master's house for wages
ev.isl_d_water.title: Someone else's water
ev.isl_d_water.text: In the night a neighbour blocked the channel and turned the water onto his own field when it was your turn to irrigate. Without water the wheat will burn up in a week.
ev.isl_d_water.dig.success: The water flowed to you, and the harvest is saved.
ev.isl_d_water.dig.failure: It ended in a fight with hoes. Now you have an enemy.
ev.isl_d_guild.title: The guild test
ev.isl_d_guild.text: The guild headman and the masters are ready to test whether you deserve a shop of your own. You must make a piece before their eyes, pay a fee and treat the whole guild to a meal.
ev.isl_d_guild.test.success: The masters passed your work from hand to hand and nodded. They tied the master's sash around your waist.
ev.isl_d_guild.test.failure: The headman found a flaw. "Come back in a year."
ev.isl_d_guild.wait: Work under a master a while longer
ev.isl_d_astrologer.title: The astrologer
ev.isl_d_astrologer.text: Before a big undertaking friends advise calling an astrologer: he will set up his astrolabe, see where Mars and Saturn stand and name a lucky day. Theologians grumble that only God knows the future.
ev.isl_d_astrologer.consult.success: The stars were favourable, and the venture went smoothly.
ev.isl_d_astrologer.consult.failure: The astrologer foretold misfortune, and you couldn't settle for a month.
ev.isl_d_book_copy.title: A dangerous book
ev.isl_d_book_copy.text: A wealthy client asks you to secretly copy a book by a philosopher whom the theologians call godless. He pays double. If it comes out, you could be accused of heresy.
ev.isl_d_trade_venture.title: A share in the voyage
ev.isl_d_trade_venture.text: Merchants are pooling money for a ship to India and China: out with cloth and glass, back with pepper, silk and porcelain. The voyage will take years. Or you can buy into a short caravan - less profit, less risk.
ev.isl_d_trade_venture.text.cordoba: Merchants are pooling money for a ship to Alexandria: out with the silks and leathers of al-Andalus, back with spices and Egyptian linen. It will take years. Or you can buy into a short convoy to Seville - less profit, less risk.
ev.isl_d_venture_news.title: The ship is back
ev.isl_d_venture_news.text: The ship has come back, battered: part of the cargo went overboard in a storm. Your share is bales of pepper in the warehouse. Prices are middling now, but may rise before Ramadan.
ev.isl_d_venture_news.hold.success: Prices soared, and you sold everything for three times as much.
ev.isl_d_venture_news.hold.failure: Another pepper ship arrived and prices collapsed.
ev.isl_d_canal.title: Clearing the canals
ev.isl_d_canal.text: Before the flood all the village men are rounded up to clear the canals and mend the dykes. It's heavy work, waist-deep in silt, but without it the water won't reach the fields.
ev.isl_d_canal.pay: Hire someone to go in your place
ev.isl_d_canal.hide: Hide with kin in the next village
ev.isl_d_canal.hide.failure: The headman found you. A fine and a beating.
ev.isl_d_poetry.title: The poets' contest
ev.isl_d_poetry.text: This evening in a noble's garden poets are competing: one begins a line, the next must take it up in the same rhyme. The winner gets a purse of silver and fame throughout the city.
ev.isl_d_poetry.text.cordoba: This evening in a noble's garden they are singing muwashshahs - the new Andalusi songs whose final verse is in the everyday tongue of the street. Poets compete; the winner gets a purse of silver and fame.
ev.isl_d_poetry.compete: Step up with your own verses
ev.isl_d_poetry.compete.success: They repeated your line until dawn. The host tossed you a purse.
ev.isl_d_poetry.compete.failure: You lost the rhyme, and the garden fell politely silent.
ev.isl_d_devshirme.title: The devshirme
ev.isl_d_devshirme.text: The sultan's collectors have come to your Greek village in Thrace. They are choosing sturdy Christian boys: the boys will be taken away, converted to Islam and trained as Janissaries or palace servants. Some such boys have risen to be viziers.
ev.isl_d_devshirme.hide.failure: They found you in a sheepfold and took you away with the others.
ev.isl_d_devshirme.note: The devshirme was the Ottoman "collection" of Christian boys (from the late 14th century) to be converted and serve the sultan. Janissaries and palace pages were drawn from them; many 16th-century viziers began this way. Townsmen were generally exempt.
ev.isl_d_devshirme_later.title: The novice boys
ev.isl_d_devshirme_later.text: For years you lived in a Turkish village, learning the language and herding someone else's sheep. Now the boys are being brought back to the capital: the strongest to the Janissary barracks, the brightest to the palace school.
ev.isl_d_devshirme_later.palace.success: The palace school teachers took you. Calligraphy, Persian, arithmetic - and your first post in the chancery.
ev.isl_d_devshirme_later.palace.failure: They judged you fit only for arms. The barracks it is.
ev.isl_d_palace_girl.title: In the palace
ev.isl_d_palace_girl.text: You have been chosen to serve in the palace quarters. Senior mistresses teach the girls reading, embroidery, music and strict order. They say those who serve diligently are freed years later with a dowry.
ev.isl_d_palace_freed.title: Freed with a dowry
ev.isl_d_palace_freed.text: You have served your years. You were given your freedom, a dowry chest and a purse - officials are eager to marry former palace servants.
ev.isl_d_palace_freed.own: Keep a house of your own
ev.isl_t_vizier.title: The vizier's favour
ev.isl_t_vizier.text: The vizier read a petition you had drafted and asked who wrote so well. Now you are summoned to the palace: to serve in his chancery, live by his favour - and, should it come to that, fall with him.
ev.isl_t_vizier_fall.title: Disgrace
ev.isl_t_vizier_fall.text: In the night the vizier was arrested, and his property is being seized for the treasury. They say his people are being hunted too. Your name is in all his papers.
ev.isl_t_vizier_fall.deny.success: They questioned you and let you go: too small a fish.
ev.isl_t_vizier_fall.deny.failure: You were thrown in prison and released penniless, without a post.
ev.isl_t_sea_voyage.title: The voyage to China
ev.isl_t_sea_voyage.text: A captain is signing up merchants for a ship sewn with palm-fibre cord: from Basra through Oman and India all the way to China. Those who return will be rich. Those who don't will end up in a story.
ev.isl_t_sea_voyage.text.cairo: A captain at Aydhab on the Red Sea is signing up merchants: through Aden to India for pepper, and for the bold, on to China. Those who return will be rich. Those who don't will end up in a story.
ev.isl_t_sea_voyage.sail.success: Three years later you came home with silk, porcelain and stories nobody believes.
ev.isl_t_sea_voyage.sail.failure: The ship broke up off the coast of India. You survived on a piece of wreckage and came home with almost nothing.
ev.isl_t_bedouin.title: A raid on the caravan
ev.isl_t_bedouin.text: On the third day of the journey horsemen burst from behind the dunes. The Bedouin leader offers to take a "fee for passage", while the drivers are already hiding their purses under the saddles.
ev.isl_t_bedouin.fight.success: The caravan fought them off. Your name is told at every campfire.
ev.isl_t_bedouin.fight.failure: A spear thrust knocked you off your camel. You came to without your purse.
ev.isl_t_heresy.title: Accused of heresy
ev.isl_t_heresy.text: An envious man has reported that in a debate you said too much about the eternity of the world. You are summoned before the qadi on a charge of zandaqa - heresy. For that you could lose everything.
ev.isl_t_heresy.defend.success: You cited so many authorities that the qadi let you go and shamed the informer.
ev.isl_t_heresy.defend.failure: The qadi did not believe you. A fine, a flogging, and half your friends stopped greeting you.
ev.isl_t_corsairs.title: Pirates
ev.isl_t_corsairs.text: The ship you were sailing on has been overtaken by a foreign galley. The captives are being sorted: for some a ransom is expected from kin and community, others will be chained to the oars.
ev.isl_t_corsairs.escape.success: You swam to shore and a month later made it home.
ev.isl_t_corsairs.escape.failure: They fished you out and beat you. The ransom had to be paid anyway.
ev.isl_t_captive_freed.title: Ransomed
ev.isl_t_captive_freed.text: The community raised the money, and merchant go-betweens ransomed you along with other captives. You stand on your home shore again - penniless, but free.
ev.isl_t_captive_freed.home: Go back to your own people
ev.isl_t_captive_freed.sea: The sea is all you know now
ev.isl_t_treasure.title: A hoard
ev.isl_t_treasure.text: Under the roots of an old tree your hoe clinked against a pot full of silver coins stamped with the profiles of ancient shahs. By law a fifth of any treasure goes to the treasury.
ev.isl_t_treasure.hide.success: You changed the coins a few at a time with different money changers. No one suspected a thing.
ev.isl_t_treasure.hide.failure: A money changer informed on you. The hoard was confiscated, with a fine on top.
ev.isl_t_treasure.mosque: Give most of it to the mosque and the poor
ev.isl_t_amir.title: The emir's retinue
ev.isl_t_amir.text: An emir watched you hold a bolting horse single-handed and offered you a place in his retinue: horse, weapons, pay. Serving an emir means campaigns - and his wars with other emirs.
ev.isl_t_amir_revolt.title: The emir rebels
ev.isl_t_amir_revolt.text: Your emir has raised his banner against the sultan. The retinue must choose: follow him to the end, or quietly slip away while there's time.
ev.isl_t_amir_revolt.loyal.success: The sultan chose to make peace, and the emir richly rewarded the loyal. Now you have your own troop and an iqta.
ev.isl_t_amir_revolt.loyal.failure: The revolt was crushed. You came back wounded, with no horse and no post.
ev.isl_t_bazaar_fire.title: Fire in the bazaar
ev.isl_t_bazaar_fire.text: In the night the next row caught fire, and the flames ran along the wooden awnings. By morning all that was left of your shop was embers and melted copper.
ev.isl_t_bazaar_fire.loan: Borrow from a moneylender and rebuild
ev.isl_t_rihla.title: The journey for knowledge
ev.isl_t_rihla.text: A famous scholar in a faraway city agrees to take you as a student. "Seek knowledge, even unto China," people say. The road is long, and who knows when you'll return.
ev.isl_t_rihla_later.title: The ijaza
ev.isl_t_rihla_later.text: Your teacher has handed you an ijaza - a sheet with a chain of teachers' names reaching back to the very first masters. Now you can gather your own circle by a pillar of the mosque.
ev.isl_t_rihla_later.court: Take a post in the divan
ev.isl_t_plague_heir.title: An inheritance after the plague
ev.isl_t_plague_heir.text: The plague carried off whole families. The qadi is sorting through wills, and it turns out you are the only living heir of distant kin: a house, a shop, debts. There are more orphans in the quarter than ever.
ev.isl_t_plague_heir.orphans: Take in an orphan and share it
ev.isl_w_muezzin.title: A voice from the minaret
ev.isl_w_muezzin.text: The congregational mosque is looking for a new muezzin, and people say your call can be heard three quarters away. But the old imam of your mosque asks you not to leave.
ev.isl_w_muezzin.compete: Try out for the great mosque
ev.isl_w_muezzin.compete.success: Now your voice wakes half the city.
ev.isl_w_muezzin.compete.failure: They chose another man, with a voice like a nightingale. You went back to your own minaret.
ev.isl_w_caravan_route.title: The shortcut
ev.isl_w_caravan_route.text: The merchants are in a hurry to reach the fair. The short way runs across waterless desert where the wells may be choked with sand. The long way follows the settled road from caravanserai to caravanserai.
ev.isl_w_caravan_route.short.success: You arrived first, and the merchants paid double.
ev.isl_w_caravan_route.short.failure: The well was dry. Half the camels died, and you barely made it yourself.
ev.isl_w_caravan_up.title: Camels of your own
ev.isl_w_caravan_up.text: Over years on the road you have saved enough to buy camels of your own and outfit caravans yourself - let others lead them across the desert now.
ev.isl_w_mamluk_freed.title: The certificate of freedom
ev.isl_w_mamluk_freed.text: The years of barracks school are behind you: Qur'an, horse, bow, lance. On graduation day your master handed you a certificate of freedom, a horse and armour. Now you are a free warrior - but loyalty to your master is a matter of honour.
ev.isl_w_mamluk_freed.richer.success: The new emir pays double and gave you men of your own.
ev.isl_w_mamluk_freed.richer.failure: You were called ungrateful. The doors of both houses closed to you.
ev.isl_w_amir.title: Emir of ten
ev.isl_w_amir.text: The sultan grants you the rank of emir of ten: your own troop, drums at your gate and a village's revenue. In the Mamluk state this is how those who later take the throne begin - and those later strangled in the Citadel.
ev.isl_w_cauldron.title: Overturned cauldrons
ev.isl_w_cauldron.text: The pay is late again. Your company comrades have overturned the pilaf cauldrons - a sign that the Janissaries refuse the sultan's bread. By evening the crowd may go to sack the viziers' houses.
ev.isl_w_cauldron.join.success: The sultan took fright and paid out wages with a bonus.
ev.isl_w_cauldron.join.failure: The ringleaders were seized. You got a beating, and your name was written down.
ev.isl_w_janissary_up.title: The company cauldron
ev.isl_w_janissary_up.text: The old çorbacı has retired, and the Janissary agha offers you his company. Everything in the Janissaries is tied to the kitchen: the commander is "the soup-giver", and the company cauldron is guarded like a banner.
ev.isl_w_janissary_wed.title: Forbidden to marry
ev.isl_w_janissary_wed.text: By the rules a Janissary does not marry while serving: his home is the barracks, his family the company. But you are in love, and many comrades have quietly set up homes in the city.
ev.isl_w_janissary_wed.marry.success: The officers pretended not to notice.
ev.isl_w_janissary_wed.marry.failure: It came out. A fine, a reprimand, and the wedding had to wait.
ev.isl_w_zij.title: Tables and horoscopes
ev.isl_w_zij.text: You have spent years refining tables of planetary motion. But your patron expects something else: a horoscope before a campaign, and a favourable one at that. The stars say otherwise.
ev.isl_w_zij.flatter: Find good fortune in the sky
ev.isl_w_comet.title: The comet
ev.isl_w_comet.text: A huge comet hangs over Istanbul, its tail spanning half the sky. At Taqi al-Din's new observatory they argue over what it portends for the sultan. Scholar friends ask your view too.
ev.isl_w_comet.note: The Great Comet of 1577 was observed across Europe and in Istanbul. Taqi al-Din, at his observatory, read it as a sign of victory over the Safavids; the war went badly, and in 1580 the observatory was demolished.
ev.isl_w_perfume.title: A scent for a lady
ev.isl_w_perfume.text: A noble lady's maid has ordered a scent no one else has: ambergris, musk, rose, a drop of aloeswood. Real ambergris costs as much as a house. Not every nose will notice a fake made of wax and resin.
ev.isl_w_perfume.fake.success: The lady was delighted and sent her friends.
ev.isl_w_perfume.fake.failure: The lady turned out to have a fine nose. Now people whisper about your shop.
ev.isl_w_perfume_up.title: A workshop of your own
ev.isl_w_perfume_up.text: There is a queue for your perfumes. You could rent a workshop with stills, hire apprentices and sell across the whole bazaar.
ev.isl_w_translator_up.title: The House of Wisdom
ev.isl_w_translator_up.text: The House of Wisdom needs another translator: Greek manuscripts have arrived - Galen, Euclid, Ptolemy. They say the caliph pays for translations in gold.
ev.isl_w_translate.title: Word or meaning
ev.isl_w_translate.text: The old translators went word by word, and the result was gibberish. The new ones - like the famous Hunayn ibn Ishaq - first compare several manuscripts and render the meaning. It takes three times as long.
ev.isl_w_coffee_open.title: A coffeehouse
ev.isl_w_coffee_open.text: The new coffeehouses are packed from morning till night: people drink bitter coffee, play backgammon, listen to poets and gossip about the viziers. The empty shop on the corner is for rent.
ev.isl_w_coffee_trouble.title: Coffee under suspicion
ev.isl_w_coffee_trouble.text: A preacher at the Friday mosque called coffee an intoxicant and coffeehouses nests of gossip and sedition. The watch has started dropping by in the evenings, listening to the talk.
ev.isl_w_coffee_trouble.bribe: Pay the watch to leave you alone
ev.isl_w_coffee_trouble.fatwa: Find a mufti who permits coffee
ev.isl_w_coffee_trouble.fatwa.success: A respected mufti wrote that coffee is permitted. You hung his fatwa by the door.
ev.isl_w_coffee_trouble.fatwa.failure: The mufti refused, and the preacher found out who had asked. You were fined.
ev.isl_w_qadi_offer.title: The office of qadi
ev.isl_w_qadi_offer.text: You are offered the post of qadi. Pious scholars have long fled this office: "Of three judges, two are in the Fire," says a tradition. But someone has to judge.
ev.isl_w_qadi_case.title: A case against an emir
ev.isl_w_qadi_case.text: A fellah widow complains that the emir's men have seized her field. The witnesses are reliable. In the evening a servant arrives from the emir with a purse and a polite hint.
ev.isl_w_qadi_case.just.success: You returned the field to the widow. The emir held his tongue, and the city remembered.
ev.isl_w_qadi_case.just.failure: The field was returned, but a month later you were dismissed. What remained was honour - and the post of imam at an old mosque.
ev.isl_w_quran_copy.title: A great commission
ev.isl_w_quran_copy.text: A noble house has commissioned a Qur'an for the mosque it is building: a large hand, gold illumination, a year's work. Not a single dot may be wrong.
ev.isl_mv_baghdad.title: The City of Peace
ev.isl_mv_baghdad.text: Merchants tell of Baghdad, the "City of Peace": the caliph's palaces, scholars from all over the world, and a literate man finds work on his very first day. The caravan leaves in a week.
ev.isl_mv_cairo.title: The new city on the Nile
ev.isl_mv_cairo.text: On the Nile rises Cairo, "the Victorious". Homes are well fed, the Nile provides, building sites and workshops pay well, and merchant ships sail from there to India and Italy alike.
ev.isl_mv_andalus.title: Go east
ev.isl_mv_andalus.text: Córdoba is not what it was: strife, foreign troops, Christian kings drawing ever nearer. People you know are selling their houses and boarding ships at Almería - for Egypt, for Syria, where it is still calm.
ev.isl_mv_mongols.title: Refugees
ev.isl_mv_mongols.text: After the Mongol sack, scholars, merchants and craftsmen are leaving Baghdad for the west - to the Mamluks in Cairo and Damascus, where there is a new caliph of the Abbasid line. Baghdad is ruled by the Ilkhans' governors.
ev.isl_mv_istanbul.title: To the sultan's capital
ev.isl_mv_istanbul.text: Now the capital is Istanbul. Sultan Selim carried off Cairo's finest craftsmen there, and business is brisk: the palace, mosques, the fleet, orders beyond counting. They say Arab craftsmen are prized there.
